text: The Patriots' turnover woes came back to haunt them Thursday night in Chicago, as they fell to the Bears 30-24 in a loss that Mike Vrabel—who counts turnover differential as one of his four pillars of team identity—will need to address if New England hopes to turn things around. Caleb Williams carved up the Patriots defense with two touchdown passes, exposing vulnerabilities that the film review from Drake Maye's performance will undoubtedly scrutinize, though there were some bright spots worth noting: Rhamondre Stevenson reached a career high in receiving yards and continues to do the little things that have kept him on pace for 100 carries for the sixth straight season. The loss marks round two going to Williams and the Bears, and the Patriots will need to find ways to eliminate the self-inflicted wounds and defensive breakdowns that proved decisive in this Thursday Night Football thriller if they're going to bounce back.
